sources.entry: mxMarkEdit - A visual editor of Markdown document, tasks and tables.

summary.one_liner: mxMarkEdit is a native macOS Markdown editor with inline formatting, an Excel-like table grid, a bibliography manager, and todo tracking, written in Lazarus/Free Pascal.
summary.what_it_does: The app edits Markdown documents with inline visual formatting, hiding markers like #, *, and ** on lines that are formatted. Each document has a hidden Excel-like grid (105 columns, 10,000 rows) for simple tables, with formulas (sum, max, min, avg, count), filtering, find, and sorting. A built-in bibliography manager uses a key-based citation system similar to BibLaTeX and can import from Zotero. Todo items support deadlines and @-assigned resources, and a todo form summarises them. It can also show a Markdown file as a slide presentation, search text across folders of .md and .csv files, and export through Pandoc if it is installed.
use_cases: writing Markdown documents on a Mac
tracking todo items with deadlines and assignees
managing a bibliography and compiling citations
keeping small data tables alongside a text
searching text across many Markdown and CSV files
exporting Markdown to Word or other formats via Pandoc
notable: Inline formatting hides Markdown markers while keeping the text formatted, similar in spirit to Emacs Org-mode
Built-in Excel-like grid per document, saved as a separate .csv file
Bibliography manager where citations are composed in their final form from table columns, with Zotero import
Presentation mode driven by keyboard shortcuts, with optional picture display
Does not use Electron; the Markdown formatting algorithm is written in Free Pascal
caveats: Runs only on Mac with Apple Silicon (M1 or later)
Not notarized by Apple, so it needs the quarantine attribute removed to open
Pandoc must be installed separately for export
